record.original_question: Justify the Ciarlet-Necas constrained minimization formulation, or an appropriate modification of it, as a model of smooth frictionless self-contact for elastic bodies, including the vanishing of tangential stress components near self-contact and the regularity of the free boundary.

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Justify the Ciarlet-Nečas minimization problem, or an appropriate modification of it, as a model of smooth self-contact.
The problem here is to construct suitable variations in the neighbourhood of a region of self-contact of a minimizer

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^3$ be a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary, representing the reference configuration of a hyperelastic body, and let $W : \Omega \times \mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ be a polyconvex stored-energy function satisfying standard coercivity and growth conditions, with $\mathbb{R}^{3\times 3}_+$ denoting the matrices with positive determinant. Consider the constrained minimization problem of Ciarlet–Nečas type: minimize the elastic energy
$$E(u) = \int_\Omega W(x, \nabla u(x))\,\mathrm{d}x$$
over the class of admissible deformations
$$\mathcal{A} = \Bigl\{ u \in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb{R}^3) : \det\nabla u > 0 \text{ a.e.,}\ \int_\Omega \det\nabla u(x)\,\mathrm{d}x \le \mathrm{vol}(u(\Omega)),\ u|_{\Gamma_0} = u_0 \Bigr\}$$
(with $p > 3$, prescribed boundary data $u_0$ on a portion $\Gamma_0 \subset \partial\Omega$), the integral inequality being the Ciarlet–Nečas global injectivity condition that allows boundary self-contact but prevents interpenetration.

Provide a rigorous justification of this minimization formulation (or a suitable modification thereof) as a model of smooth frictionless self-contact. Specifically, prove that for a minimizer $u^*$:
(a) the tangential components of the Cauchy stress vector vanish on the deformed self-contact set (no friction);
(b) the free boundary separating the regions of self-contact from the non-contact region is regular (e.g., smooth or locally a $C^1$ hypersurface) under appropriate smoothness hypotheses on $W$ and on the data;
(c) construct admissible variations supported in a neighborhood of the self-contact region needed to derive the corresponding Euler–Lagrange/variational inequality conditions.
artifact.status_search_result: The Ciarlet–Nečas formulation (1987) guarantees existence of energy minimizers satisfying the global injectivity condition, but the variational/free-boundary characterization of frictionless self-contact (vanishing tangential stress, regularity of the free boundary) has not been fully established. Recent works (e.g., Krömer–Valdman, ARMA 2021) have refined the admissible class and injectivity properties, but a complete justification including stress conditions and free-boundary regularity remains an open program.

status_evidence.title: Injectivity and self-contact in nonlinear elasticity
status_evidence.snippet: The Ciarlet–Nečas minimization with the global injectivity integral inequality, proving existence in W^{1,p}, p>3.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the original existence result but does not derive contact stress conditions or free-boundary regularity.

status_evidence.title: On the Self-Contact Problem in Nonlinear Elasticity
status_evidence.snippet: Defines a new class of admissible deformations enabling frictionless self-contact and forbidding self-intersection, proving homeomorphism properties of orientation-preserving Sobolev maps.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on modifying the Ciarlet–Nečas framework, indicating the original justification problem is still being pursued.
